title: Growth, Photosynthesis, and Cellular Respiration Core Test
description: Core practice for growth factors, photosynthesis, cellular respiration, matter, and energy flow.

questions.prompt: Two genetically similar bean plants are grown for two weeks. One gets light and water, while the other gets little light. Which claim is best supported if the low-light plant grows less?
questions.questionText: Two genetically similar bean plants are grown for two weeks. One gets light and water, while the other gets little light. Which claim is best supported if the low-light plant grows less?
options: Light availability can affect growth by affecting sugar production.
Genes never affect growth.
Plants grow less only because soil disappears.
Light changes water into new genes.
questions.correctAnswer: Light availability can affect growth by affecting sugar production.
questions.explanation: Light is needed for photosynthesis, which produces sugars used for growth.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of photosynthesis in plants?
questions.questionText: What is the main role of photosynthesis in plants?
options: to use light energy to make sugar molecules
to break bones into minerals
to carry nerve signals
to remove all matter from cells
questions.correctAnswer: to use light energy to make sugar molecules
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy, carbon dioxide, and water to make sugars.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of cellular respiration?
questions.questionText: What is the main role of cellular respiration?
options: to release usable energy from food molecules
to make sunlight
to make a cell wall disappear
to sort animals into groups
questions.correctAnswer: to release usable energy from food molecules
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration releases usable energy from food molecules in cells.

questions.prompt: Which model correctly shows energy flow in a plant cell?
questions.questionText: Which model correctly shows energy flow in a plant cell?
options: light -> photosynthesis -> sugar -> cellular respiration -> usable energy
sugar -> light -> water disappears -> no cell work
cell wall -> sunlight -> nucleus -> oxygen only
usable energy -> photosynthesis stops -> sugar destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: light -> photosynthesis -> sugar -> cellular respiration -> usable energy
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis stores energy in sugars; cellular respiration releases usable energy from those food molecules.

questions.prompt: Which materials are used during photosynthesis?
questions.questionText: Which materials are used during photosynthesis?
options: carbon dioxide and water, with light energy
oxygen and sugar only
muscle and bone
sound and heat only
questions.correctAnswer: carbon dioxide and water, with light energy
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide, water, and light energy.

questions.prompt: A sealed plant chamber has less carbon dioxide after several hours in bright light. Which process most likely used the carbon dioxide?
questions.questionText: A sealed plant chamber has less carbon dioxide after several hours in bright light. Which process most likely used the carbon dioxide?
options: photosynthesis
hearing
digestion in the stomach
bone growth only
questions.correctAnswer: photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Plants do not need cellular respiration because they do photosynthesis." Which response is most accurate?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Plants do not need cellular respiration because they do photosynthesis." Which response is most accurate?
options: Plants also use cellular respiration to release usable energy from sugars.
Plants cannot make sugars.
Only animal cells need energy.
Photosynthesis and respiration are the same process.
questions.correctAnswer: Plants also use cellular respiration to release usable energy from sugars.
questions.explanation: Plants make sugars through photosynthesis and use cellular respiration to release usable energy from food molecules.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports that water shortage can reduce plant growth?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports that water shortage can reduce plant growth?
options: Plants with equal light but less water are shorter after two weeks.
Plants in different pots have different labels.
The classroom has windows.
A ruler is made of plastic.
questions.correctAnswer: Plants with equal light but less water are shorter after two weeks.
questions.explanation: This comparison isolates water as a factor affecting growth.

questions.prompt: A model shows sugar molecules being rearranged in cells and usable energy being released. Which process does the model show?
questions.questionText: A model shows sugar molecules being rearranged in cells and usable energy being released. Which process does the model show?
options: cellular respiration
photosynthesis only
competition
information processing
questions.correctAnswer: cellular respiration
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration rearranges food molecules and releases usable energy.

questions.prompt: Which statement best separates matter and energy?
questions.questionText: Which statement best separates matter and energy?
options: Matter is the stuff molecules are made of; energy flows as it is stored and released.
Matter and energy are exactly the same thing.
Energy has mass but matter does not.
Matter disappears whenever energy flows.
questions.correctAnswer: Matter is the stuff molecules are made of; energy flows as it is stored and released.
questions.explanation: Matter cycles through systems, while energy flows and changes form.

questions.prompt: A plant grows more slowly in soil lacking key minerals, even with enough light and water. Which explanation best fits?
questions.questionText: A plant grows more slowly in soil lacking key minerals, even with enough light and water. Which explanation best fits?
options: Growth needs materials from the environment as well as energy.
Light is never important for growth.
Minerals replace the need for cells.
Plants get all matter from sunlight.
questions.correctAnswer: Growth needs materials from the environment as well as energy.
questions.explanation: Growth depends on matter and energy resources, including nutrients needed to build cells.

questions.prompt: Which cause/effect chain best explains why a shaded plant may have less growth?
questions.questionText: Which cause/effect chain best explains why a shaded plant may have less growth?
options: less light -> less photosynthesis -> less sugar available -> less growth
less light -> more sugar -> more growth
less light -> no cells -> instant death always
shade -> more carbon dioxide made from sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: less light -> less photosynthesis -> less sugar available -> less growth
questions.explanation: The chain connects the environmental factor to the process and then the growth result.

questions.prompt: Yeast cells release more gas when sugar is available. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: Yeast cells release more gas when sugar is available. Which claim is best supported?
options: Sugar can provide food molecules for cellular respiration.
Sugar prevents all cell activity.
Yeast cells do not use energy.
Gas production proves photosynthesis happened.
questions.correctAnswer: Sugar can provide food molecules for cellular respiration.
questions.explanation: Yeast can use sugar in cellular respiration, releasing gas as evidence of the process.

questions.prompt: Which organism is most likely able to use photosynthesis?
questions.questionText: Which organism is most likely able to use photosynthesis?
options: algae in a sunny pond
a running dog
a mushroom in dark soil
a classroom desk
questions.correctAnswer: algae in a sunny pond
questions.explanation: Algae can photosynthesize when light is available.

questions.prompt: A student claims plants get most of their food from soil. Which evidence best corrects the claim?
questions.questionText: A student claims plants get most of their food from soil. Which evidence best corrects the claim?
options: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make sugars during photosynthesis.
Soil is usually brown.
Roots can hold a plant in place.
Some plants grow in pots.
questions.correctAnswer: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make sugars during photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Soil provides minerals and support, but plants make sugars through photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: A plant is moved from bright light to darkness. Which outcome is most likely after several days if other conditions stay the same?
questions.questionText: A plant is moved from bright light to darkness. Which outcome is most likely after several days if other conditions stay the same?
options: The plant makes less sugar by photosynthesis.
The plant makes more sugar from light.
The plant stops containing cells.
The plant no longer needs energy.
questions.correctAnswer: The plant makes less sugar by photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Less light means less energy available for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which table result best supports the idea that light affects photosynthesis?
questions.questionText: Which table result best supports the idea that light affects photosynthesis?
options: bright light: many oxygen bubbles; dim light: few oxygen bubbles
red pot: 12 cm tall; blue pot: 12 cm tall
Monday: cloudy; Tuesday: sunny
plant A: green; plant B: green
questions.correctAnswer: bright light: many oxygen bubbles; dim light: few oxygen bubbles
questions.explanation: Oxygen bubbles can be evidence of photosynthesis, and the pattern changes with light level.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows matter cycling through living systems?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows matter cycling through living systems?
options: carbon dioxide enters plants, sugar becomes body material or food, wastes and decay return matter
sunlight becomes soil and never changes
energy cycles forever without loss
cells make matter disappear during growth
questions.correctAnswer: carbon dioxide enters plants, sugar becomes body material or food, wastes and decay return matter
questions.explanation: Matter moves through organisms and the environment; it does not simply disappear.

questions.prompt: A student says, "If a plant grows taller, only energy was added." What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says, "If a plant grows taller, only energy was added." What is the best correction?
options: Growth also requires matter to build new cell material.
Growth requires no materials.
Energy has weight and becomes the whole plant.
Cells do not matter in growth.
questions.correctAnswer: Growth also requires matter to build new cell material.
questions.explanation: New growth requires matter to build more cell structures.

questions.prompt: Which question would best test whether carbon dioxide affects plant sugar production?
questions.questionText: Which question would best test whether carbon dioxide affects plant sugar production?
options: Do plants with different carbon dioxide levels produce different amounts of sugar when light and water are controlled?
Which plant has the prettiest leaf?
Can a plant survive in any classroom?
Do all pots weigh the same before planting?
questions.correctAnswer: Do plants with different carbon dioxide levels produce different amounts of sugar when light and water are controlled?
questions.explanation: A fair test changes carbon dioxide while controlling other major factors.

questions.prompt: A model shows oxygen entering animal cells and carbon dioxide leaving them. Which process is most directly connected to this exchange?
questions.questionText: A model shows oxygen entering animal cells and carbon dioxide leaving them. Which process is most directly connected to this exchange?
options: cellular respiration
photosynthesis in animal cells
pollination
erosion
questions.correctAnswer: cellular respiration
questions.explanation: Animal cells use oxygen in cellular respiration and release carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects inherited factors and environment to growth?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects inherited factors and environment to growth?
options: Genes can influence growth potential, while resources affect how that potential develops.
Environment is the only factor in every growth difference.
Inherited information cannot affect living things.
Sunlight replaces inherited information.
questions.correctAnswer: Genes can influence growth potential, while resources affect how that potential develops.
questions.explanation: Growth is influenced by both inherited information and environmental resources.

questions.prompt: Two plants have the same light and water, but one variety is naturally shorter. Which factor best explains the difference?
questions.questionText: Two plants have the same light and water, but one variety is naturally shorter. Which factor best explains the difference?
options: inherited information
different sunlight
different water
lack of cells
questions.correctAnswer: inherited information
questions.explanation: If environmental factors are controlled, inherited differences may explain the growth pattern.

questions.prompt: Which choice best explains why animals depend on photosynthesis, even though animal cells do not photosynthesize?
questions.questionText: Which choice best explains why animals depend on photosynthesis, even though animal cells do not photosynthesize?
options: Photosynthesis makes food molecules that enter food webs.
Animal cells turn sunlight directly into bones.
Photosynthesis happens only inside nerves.
Animals do not need food molecules.
questions.correctAnswer: Photosynthesis makes food molecules that enter food webs.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis produces sugars that support producers and food webs that animals depend on.

questions.prompt: A class compares radish growth in full nutrients and low nutrients. Which result would best support the claim that nutrients affect growth?
questions.questionText: A class compares radish growth in full nutrients and low nutrients. Which result would best support the claim that nutrients affect growth?
options: full nutrients: taller average plants; low nutrients: shorter average plants
both groups watered at the same time
both groups used the same tray color
full nutrients had labels written in pen
questions.correctAnswer: full nutrients: taller average plants; low nutrients: shorter average plants
questions.explanation: A consistent height difference between nutrient conditions supports the claim.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes energy in photosynthesis and respiration?
questions.questionText: Which statement best describes energy in photosynthesis and respiration?
options: Photosynthesis stores energy in sugars; respiration releases usable energy from sugars.
Both processes only destroy matter.
Photosynthesis releases energy from sugar in all animals.
Respiration stores sunlight inside chloroplasts.
questions.correctAnswer: Photosynthesis stores energy in sugars; respiration releases usable energy from sugars.
questions.explanation: The two processes are connected but have different roles in energy flow.

questions.prompt: A pond plant makes fewer oxygen bubbles when a shade screen is added. Which explanation best fits?
questions.questionText: A pond plant makes fewer oxygen bubbles when a shade screen is added. Which explanation best fits?
options: The shade screen reduced light, lowering the rate of photosynthesis.
The shade screen added more carbon dioxide.
Oxygen bubbles prove the plant stopped being alive.
The plant started using sound instead of light.
questions.correctAnswer: The shade screen reduced light, lowering the rate of photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Reduced light can reduce photosynthesis, and fewer oxygen bubbles are evidence of that change.

questions.prompt: Which model revision would improve this chain: light -> growth?
questions.questionText: Which model revision would improve this chain: light -> growth?
options: light -> photosynthesis -> sugar molecules -> cell materials and energy needs -> growth
light -> no matter -> no cells -> growth
light -> bones -> nerves -> growth
light -> labels -> pots -> growth
questions.correctAnswer: light -> photosynthesis -> sugar molecules -> cell materials and energy needs -> growth
questions.explanation: A stronger model shows the processes between the cause and the growth result.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would weaken the claim that light alone determines plant growth?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would weaken the claim that light alone determines plant growth?
options: Two plants with equal light grow differently when one lacks water.
A plant in light is green.
A lamp is placed above a plant.
A ruler can measure plant height.
questions.correctAnswer: Two plants with equal light grow differently when one lacks water.
questions.explanation: If water changes growth when light is equal, light is not the only factor.

questions.prompt: Which final explanation best shows fundamental understanding of growth and energy flow?
questions.questionText: Which final explanation best shows fundamental understanding of growth and energy flow?
options: Organisms grow when cells have inherited instructions plus matter and energy resources; photosynthesis stores energy in sugars and respiration releases usable energy.
Growth happens only when organisms are placed near windows.
Energy and matter disappear after photosynthesis.
Respiration is needed only by animals that run.
questions.correctAnswer: Organisms grow when cells have inherited instructions plus matter and energy resources; photosynthesis stores energy in sugars and respiration releases usable energy.
questions.explanation: This explanation connects inherited factors, resources, matter, photosynthesis, respiration, and growth.
